requirement: Describe a prospective, unblinded, two-arm parallel community trial across California, Illinois, Iowa, Puerto Rico and Texas, comparing the six-week Abriendo Caminos family curriculum with a non-intervention control condition in low-income, low-literacy Hispanic-heritage families containing at least one child aged 6-18 years.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the target families, five locations, six-session curriculum, randomized controlled design and follow-up schedule.

requirement: Confirm that whole families, not individual children or parents, are the randomization units; then prespecify the allocation ratio, sequence generation, any site or cycle stratification, concealment and implementation roles, none of which is fully defined in the source pair.

evidence.text: The protocol says whole families are recruited and a randomized controlled design is used but gives no allocation procedure.
The plan says control and intervention groups will be randomly assigned but does not define the unit or method.

requirement: Treat the trial as open label and document whether anthropometric measurement, questionnaire scoring or analysis can be blinded; do not infer masking from randomization.

evidence.text: The face-to-face curriculum and control procedures imply visible assignment, while no assessor or analyst masking is stated.

requirement: Define the family, parent and child analysis records and rules for families with multiple eligible children or participating adults, linking every repeated child outcome to its randomized family without treating relatives as independent observations.

evidence.text: Whole families with one or more eligible children participate and parent and child measures are collected.
The plan nests time within child and child within family but omits record-selection rules.

requirement: Define a primary intention-to-treat or full-analysis population containing all randomized families and their eligible children according to assigned condition, with explicit rules for consent withdrawal, ineligible records, absent baseline data and families providing no postbaseline measurements.

evidence.text: The protocol defines recruitment and repeated data collection but no analysis population.
The plan describes models and drop-out summaries without defining an analysis set.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy outcome as change from baseline through six months in child BMI-for-age percentile, with lower or non-increasing percentile representing benefit, and identify the six-month between-arm comparison as the primary timepoint.

evidence.text: The protocol defines prevention of excessive weight gain through six months and the three measurement times.
The plan identifies child BMI percentile and stable, maintained or negative change from baseline as the primary outcome.

requirement: Specify how height and weight produce BMI and how sex and exact age map BMI to a named pediatric growth-reference percentile, including implausible-value checks and the rule when a participant reaches age 18 during follow-up.

evidence.text: The target spans ages 6-18 and the outcome is healthy weight, but no BMI-percentile derivation algorithm is supplied.
The plan names BMI percentile but does not define its calculation.

requirement: Resolve whether primary success is a continuous adjusted mean difference in BMI-percentile change or an individual binary stable-or-negative-change responder comparison; do not silently combine the reference plan's continuous mixed model with its threshold-like success wording.

evidence.text: The outcome wording invokes stable or negative individual change while the primary analysis specifies mixed modeling of BMI percentiles.

requirement: Map assessments to baseline before intervention, immediately after the six-week program and six months after program completion; define operational visit windows and how out-of-window observations are assigned.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the three assessment occasions but no visit windows.

requirement: Define secondary outcomes for increased fruit, vegetable and legume consumption, reduced sugar-sweetened-beverage consumption, increased daily physical-activity minutes and improved family-mealtime organization, preserving the stated directional thresholds only after their units and assessment horizons are verified.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the four main behavioral outcome constructs.
The plan gives 0.5-serving and 10-minute target changes, including a likely unit typo that requires confirmation.

requirement: For every behavioral outcome, name the respondent, instrument version, item-to-score algorithm, unit, direction of benefit and valid-range rule; at minimum reconcile parent-versus-child dietary measures, the Family Ritual Questionnaire and the long-form International Physical Activity Questionnaire.

evidence.text: The protocol names dietary, family-ritual and physical-activity instruments but does not give executable scoring rules.

requirement: Define the primary six-month treatment-policy estimand and strategies for missed workshops, partial family participation, control receipt of health-promotion material after the third survey, withdrawal, loss to follow-up and other intercurrent events.

evidence.text: The family intervention and follow-up create adherence and attrition events, but no estimand is defined.
Control families receive health-promotion material only after the six-month survey.

requirement: Complete the planned longitudinal mixed model for child BMI percentile with fixed effects for assigned condition, categorical visit and condition-by-visit interaction, appropriate baseline adjustment, and random effects or residual covariance for repeated visits within child and children within family; prespecify the six-month contrast and degrees-of-freedom method.

evidence.text: The plan specifies random effects for time within child and child within family plus treatment-by-time interaction, but omits a complete model and contrast.
The protocol supplies the outcome and repeated visit structure.

requirement: Account for the five implementation sites and staggered cycles in estimation and inference, specifying fixed versus random site effects, any treatment-by-site assessment, sparse-site fallback and whether randomization was stratified within site or cycle.

evidence.text: Implementation spans five culturally distinct sites and is staggered, but the analysis treatment of site and cycle is absent.

requirement: Separate the confirmatory randomized treatment-effect model from the proposed multilevel mixture model: define the latter's level, latent classes, candidate baseline predictors, class-number search, identifiability, convergence and inferential purpose, and label it exploratory unless prospectively frozen.

evidence.text: The primary-analysis section proposes a multilevel mixture model and selection of the best-fitting interpretable model without an executable specification.

requirement: Do not choose a confirmatory model, transformation or predictor set from observed fit alone; prespecify the primary parameterization and any transformation rules, and confine AIC, BIC, scatterplot-driven transformations and variable-selection algorithms to sensitivity or exploratory work.
acceptable_values: random tie-breaking excluded from primary analysis

evidence.text: The plan proposes scatterplot-based transformation, AIC/BIC model selection, variable-selection algorithms and random tie breaking.

requirement: Prespecify any covariates used in the primary model without significance-driven selection; distinguish child- and parent-level education, acculturation, food-consumption and social-support variables and retain design factors regardless of observed imbalance.

evidence.text: The plan lists parent and child independent variables but does not state which enter the confirmatory model.

requirement: Define proportionate safety monitoring for a low-risk behavioral trial, including the safety population, adverse-event and serious-adverse-event definitions, attribution and summaries by assigned condition, with separate capture of injuries or medical events during food preparation and physical activity.

evidence.text: The intervention includes cooking and physical activity but the public protocol extract and analysis plan provide no safety-analysis specification.

requirement: For each secondary outcome, select a distribution-appropriate repeated-measures model, define its effect measure and six-month contrast, preserve family and child dependence, and treat parent-level mixture and tertiary association analyses as exploratory.

evidence.text: Secondary outcomes are to use techniques like the primary outcome, with a parent-level mixture model and tertiary random-effects associations, but details are absent.

requirement: Specify handling of intermittently missing items, missing visits and family dropout under an explicit missing-at-random assumption, including instrument-specific scoring thresholds, likelihood contribution and auxiliary variables; do not treat a separate dropout table as missing-data analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol anticipates attrition and describes retention effort without analysis rules.
The plan mentions dropouts and maximum likelihood but gives no missing-data assumptions or scoring rules.

requirement: Add a prespecified missing-not-at-random sensitivity analysis for the primary outcome, such as family-clustered delta-adjusted multiple imputation or a tipping-point analysis, and a clearly labeled adherence-based supplementary analysis that does not replace intention-to-treat inference.

evidence.text: Retention mechanisms imply anticipated attrition, but no robustness analysis is supplied.
The plan contains no MNAR or adherence sensitivity analysis.

requirement: Protect one prespecified six-month BMI-percentile comparison at two-sided alpha 0.05 and define whether and how family-wise error is controlled across the four secondary outcome families, repeated visits, subgroup or latent-class analyses; otherwise label them exploratory with confidence intervals.
acceptable_values: secondary multiplicity method or exploratory label

evidence.text: The plan applies two-sided 5% tests broadly across primary, secondary and tertiary analyses without a hierarchy or multiplicity rule.

requirement: Reconcile the prospective sample-size target before freezing the SAP: protocol page 10 says 250 whole families total, whereas reference page 3 and registry metadata say 250 intervention plus 250 control families. State the family-level randomized target, per-site and per-arm allocation, oversampling convention and analysis unit without substituting actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol states that whole families n=250 will be recruited.
The plan states 50 intervention families per site plus the same number of controls, 500 total, with five-family oversampling per cycle and 20% attrition.

requirement: Reproduce a primary-outcome power calculation tied to the adjudicated randomized family count, BMI-percentile effect and variance, family and site correlation, repeated measures, attrition, two-sided alpha and intended mixed model; do not use the food-serving calculations as proof of BMI-endpoint power.

evidence.text: The plan reports 0.90 power for BMI percentile and separate food-serving power claims but omits effect, variance and dependence inputs needed to reproduce the primary calculation.

requirement: Keep the three-page Statistical Analyses Plan annotation-only and require registry plus original IRB or grant evidence binding both same-title, same-investigator 2018-04-06 files to NCT03505658/15503 and confirming that the during-conduct versions were outcome-uninformed; exclude the family if that chain cannot be established.

evidence.text: The protocol cover gives title, investigator and 2018-04-06 date but no NCT or protocol number.
The separate plan repeats the same cover identity and date but also omits NCT and protocol number.
